rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 10 'Shape the execution: naming the skill, isolating the work' (lines 155-172), line 157: 'One of them is psychology dressed as mechanics, which is why it sits here rather than under interaction.' 'Them' resolves in-chunk to the six execution moves just named in the same sentence, but WHICH ONE is 'psychology dressed as mechanics' is never identified -- not on this slide (Skill by name / Subagent isolation both read as mechanical, neither as psychology) and never closed on any later slide either (chunks 11-12: Parallel-stance dispatch, Preamble suppressor, Research before ask, Fail loud not fabricate all pass without a callback naming which one was meant). Matches rule 1's 'never named' forward-reference category verbatim (the rule's own example: 'before the three things get named' pointing at a later slide). Harm is real and present: a deck reader is left holding an open question the page never answers.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name the entry directly in the sentence (e.g. 'Preamble suppressor is the one that's psychology dressed as mechanics') or cut the aside -- the family doesn't need the taxonomy justification to function as a lookup.

rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for cross-file positional phrasing ('the opening lecture said', 'earlier module', etc.) -> 0 hits. The 'Example:' lines closing each three-move pattern (chunk 22 line 322; chunk 23 lines 340/347/354; chunk 24 line 365) name real prompts by REGISTRY KEY (e.g. 'compound-and-close-1', 'ae101-m3-sharpen-skill') -- more precise than naming by title, squarely inside the navigational-pointer carve-out, never located by file position. chunk 14 'Shape the interaction: pacing the questions' (lines 217-232) carries two entries: 'Batched, not dumped' (line 219, matches the header exactly) and 'Push-back invitation' (line 225: 'Names the moment the agent should expect disagreement, and tells it not to soften') -- which is about permission to disagree, not about pacing or counting questions. rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Broaden the header to cover both moves (e.g. 'pacing the questions, inviting the pushback') or give Push-back invitation its own heading.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every hit of surface/forcing function/beat/mood/compendium/firing/Connections in the body. Line 39 ('The surface the skill called out harder than I would have') and line 199 ('surface a stuck state') use 'surface' as the ordinary access-control / engineering verb-noun the rule explicitly exempts, not curriculum-authorial 'writing surface'. Lines 303/305/307 ('...concreteness forcing function') use 'forcing function' as the coined move-name -- the rule's own audience-register carve-out clears this term by name for AE101 engineer ICs ('forcing function is ordinary shop vocabulary'). Line 237 ('find what's still surface') and line 309 ('Quote the specific session beat') sit inside ITALICISED quoted example-prompt fragments -- the file's own contract (line 11; maintainer 'Voice rotation' note) declares every italicised fragment a verbatim/representative quote from a real prompt; rewriting them to dodge 'surface'/'beat' would falsify an attested quote, which the dispatch preamble instructs against filing as a REVISE for. No hits at all for 'compendium', 'firing', 'mood', or 'Connections' as a proper noun anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This page is explicitly named in the rule's own lookup-page carve-out ('...prompt-anatomy.md, whose maintainer block declares the shape as its voice contract...'). Line 11 and the maintainer block's 'Voice rotation' note both declare the per-entry shape as deliberate: 'bold lead-in carrying both definition and the start/first beat of the why; plain continuation; italicised quote.' Sampled entries across the file (lines 21, 47, 143, 265) -- bold consistently spans 1-2 short declarative clauses (definition + opening of the why), never a whole paragraph, applied uniformly by design across all 33 entries, not sporadically. Rule-question for the maintainer, not a defect: the carve-out's closing sentence ('Bold never crosses the first sentence boundary; multi-sentence bold is the violation shape here') reads narrower than the two-sentence lead this exact file uses by declared contract and is cited as the carve-out's own example for. Cutting every entry to one grammatical sentence would rewrite the file's attested voice for no comprehension gain -- the harm the rule guards against (bold-as-decoration diluting a real handle) is not present, since every bolded span stays a single tight lead unit, never a whole entry. Suggest tightening the clause to 'one bolded lead-in UNIT (1-2 short sentences where the page's own contract declares that shape)' rather than a literal single-sentence cap.
